page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E6.Ax.192 is an x86_64 bare metal instance powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 192 physical cores with dedicated CPU allocation, supporting simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core for a total of 384 vCPUs. The server is equipped with 1536 GB of system RAM, maintaining a consistent memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU across the entire node.

For localized high-speed input and output, the configuration bundles a 1920 GB NVMe solid-state drive. Unlike standard virtualized instances, the absence of a hypervisor allows bare metal workloads to interface directly with physical components, mitigating virtualization jitter and I/O latency. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not contain discrete graphics processing units, centering resource availability entirely on high-throughput central processing and main memory.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the consolidation of 192 physical cores into a single physical chassis maximizes compute density while maintaining a standard general-purpose memory ratio. This design yields cost-effective resource consolidation for deployments where dividing large workloads across smaller virtual instances would otherwise incur hypervisor and networking overhead. BM.Standard.E6.Ax.192 is suitable for running bare metal hypervisors, dense container orchestration clusters, large-scale relational or in-memory databases, distributed ETL pipelines, and compute-heavy batch processing jobs.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E6.Ax.192 is a bare metal compute instance engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads requiring dedicated hardware resources. The server is built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. It provides 192 physical cores and 384 execution threads with simultaneous multithreading enabled across two threads per core. System memory totals 1536 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per thread. Local high-speed storage is provided via a bundled 1920 GB NVMe solid-state drive, while the configuration omits discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs. With dedicated bare metal access, it bypasses hypervisor scheduling contention, delivering predictable compute and memory bandwidth at high operational density. This infrastructure profile is well suited for memory-intensive web serving fleets, enterprise database servers, high-volume container hosting, and distributed data analytics pipelines.
